title: Reverse-Audience Building
author: Josue Valles
summary: Josue Valles argues that professionals who say they want a large following actually want clients, referrals, recognition or speaking invitations, none of which require a huge audience. An audience, he says, is a proxy for reputation, and chasing one tends to mean performing for strangers and following tips from people whose only skill is audience building. His alternative is reverse-audience building: list 30 to 50 people you admire or who could open a door, and create content just for them before publishing anything. He gives two examples, a carousel of Justin Welsh's hundred best posts that began a relationship with him, and an interview series with founders where about 90 percent agreed to a follow-up video. The approach looks slower because follower counts barely move, but opportunities come from people, and relationships with well-connected individuals eventually bring their peers and followers too.
points: A big audience is a reputation heuristic and does not automatically produce clients, referrals or stage invitations.
Start by naming 30 to 50 specific people and creating work for them, giving them a reason to know you without asking for anything.
Effective forms include breaking down someone's work, writing a case study about their company, or inviting them into an interview series.
The payoff is slower but compounds, since one well-connected relationship opens doors to their clients, peers and followers.
quotes: An audience doesn’t automatically give you clients or referrals or a spot on a big stage. An audience is a proxy for reputation.
So you might get the big number and still not get the clients, the referrals or the invitations to speak.
Write down a list of 30, 40, or 50 people you deeply admire, you’d love working with, or who could open a door for you. Then, start creating just for them.
I call this “reverse-audience” building because you’re building your audience before you publish anything.
The idea is that you give them a reason to get to know you, without asking them for anything.
Your follower count barely moves while you’re working one person at a time. But the point was always the opportunities, and opportunities come from people.
Plus, AI is making content abundant, so this type of content becomes more valuable every year.
